name: Massachusetts
note: Massachusetts registers deaths at town level: the attending physician, a hospital medical officer or the medical examiner furnishes the certificate, the undertaker completes it and returns it to the local board of health, which countersigns the burial permit and transmits the certificate to the town clerk for recording. Clerks record in the state registrar's centralized automated database and send original death records to the state registrar monthly. Every cremation needs a medical examiner's view and authorisation. The town clerk sends a monthly list of deceased adult residents to the registrars of voters, and copies the record to the clerk of the decedent's home town. Death records are not among the restricted records, so certified copies are open.

citations.title: Death certificates; issuance; declaration of death by nurse, nurse practitioner or physician's assistant
citations.quote: shall immediately furnish for registration a standard certificate of death

citations.title: Declaration of death by registered nurse
citations.quote: may declare such person dead; provided, however, that said nurse first makes a reasonable effort to contact the attending physician or medical examiner

citations.title: Declaration of death by nurse practitioner
citations.quote: A nurse practitioner, after the death of a person who was a patient under the care of such nurse practitioner, may declare the person dead.

citations.title: Penalties
citations.quote: neglecting or refusing to furnish a certificate as provided in section nine or making a false statement therein, shall forfeit not more than fifty dollars

citations.title: Reporting deaths to the chief medical examiner
citations.quote: It shall be the duty of any person having knowledge of a death which occurs under the circumstances enumerated in this paragraph

citations.title: Cremation or burial at sea; view by medical examiner
citations.quote: view the body and make personal inquiry concerning the cause and manner of death of any person whose body is intended for cremation

citations.title: Notification of births and deaths
citations.quote: the oldest next of kin of a deceased person in the town where the death occurs shall, within five days thereafter, cause notice thereof

citations.title: Notification of deaths by institutions
citations.quote: shall, on or before the fifth day of each month, give notice to the town clerk of every birth and death

citations.title: Penalty for failure to report births and deaths
citations.quote: neglecting so to do for ten days after the time limited therefor

citations.title: Duties of undertakers
citations.quote: Every undertaker or other person in charge of a funeral shall forthwith obtain the physician's or officer's certificate required by section nine

citations.title: Burial permits; permits for removal of bodies; certificates of death
citations.quote: No such permit shall be issued until there shall have been delivered to such board, agent or clerk

citations.quote: shall forthwith countersign it and transmit it to the clerk of the town for registration

citations.quote: The state registrar shall establish, maintain and operate a centralized, automated database for the system of vital records and statistics

citations.title: Automated database — death certificate entry
citations.quote: for licensed health professionals and licensed funeral directors to enter information required for standard certificates of death

citations.title: Death records; state registrar; originals

citations.quote: shall, on the first day of every month, and also two days before every election, transmit to the registrars of voters a list

steps.title: Physician, nurse, nurse practitioner or PA declares death
steps.who: A physician; a registered nurse employed by a home health agency, hospice, nursing home or PACE program for an anticipated death there; a nurse practitioner or physician assistant for their own patient.
steps.summary: A non-physician pronouncement is made in writing on a DPH form under penalty of perjury, after trying to reach the attending physician or medical examiner, who must be told where the body has been taken.

steps.title: Report listed deaths to the chief medical examiner
steps.who: Any person with knowledge of the death.
steps.trigger: Criminal violence, accident, suicide, suspicious circumstances, unlawful abortion, occupational causes, death in custody or institution, suspected abuse, and other listed cases.
steps.summary: The medical examiner then issues a medical examiner's certificate of death instead of the physician.

steps.title: Medical examiner views every body intended for cremation
steps.who: A medical examiner or forensic investigator designated by the chief medical examiner, for a fee.
steps.trigger: Intended cremation or burial at sea.
steps.summary: Cremation is authorised only when no further examination or judicial inquiry is needed, giving an independent check on every cremation case.

steps.title: Physician furnishes the death certificate to the undertaker
steps.who: The physician who attended the last illness, the physician declaring death, a hospital medical officer, a physician assistant, or the medical examiner.
steps.summary: The certifier states the cause of death and furnishes the standard certificate to the undertaker or family. Failure or a false statement is punishable by a forfeit of up to $50. Health professionals enter certificates in the state's automated database.

steps.title: Householder and next of kin give notice of the death
steps.who: The householder where the death occurred and the oldest next of kin in the town; institutions report monthly to the town clerk.
steps.summary: Notice goes to the local board of health (or the town clerk where the selectmen are the board). Neglect for ten days beyond the limit carries a nominal forfeit.

steps.title: Undertaker returns the completed certificate to the board of health
steps.who: The undertaker or other person in charge of the funeral.
steps.trigger: Receipt of the physician's or medical examiner's certificate.
steps.summary: The undertaker adds the personal particulars required by § 1 and returns the certificate to the local board of health or its agent; funeral directors enter certificates in the automated database.

steps.title: Burial permit issued on the certificate; board transmits it to the town clerk
steps.who: The local board of health or its agent (or the town clerk where there is no board).
steps.trigger: Delivery of the statement of facts and the physician's or medical examiner's certificate.
steps.summary: No body may be buried, otherwise disposed of or removed without a permit, and no permit issues without the certificate; the board countersigns and sends the certificate to the town clerk for registration.

steps.title: Town clerk records in the state database and sends originals to the state registrar
steps.who: The clerk of the city or town where the death occurred.

deadline.text: on or before the tenth day of the following month

steps.summary: Clerks record deaths in the state registrar's centralized automated database and transmit original death records monthly, keeping a certified copy.

steps.title: Certified copies from any town clerk or the state registrar
steps.who: Any applicant; death records are not among the restricted records (out-of-wedlock and abnormal-sex births, fetal deaths, certain marriage records).
steps.summary: Any town clerk can issue a certified copy from the central database regardless of where the death was recorded.

steps.title: Copy of the death record to the town of residence
steps.who: The clerk of the town of death, to the clerk of the decedent's home town (and the town of burial of a war veteran).
steps.trigger: Deaths recorded in the preceding month of residents of other Massachusetts towns.

deadline.text: forthwith, for deaths recorded during the preceding month

steps.summary: The home town's clerk thereby learns of residents' deaths elsewhere in the Commonwealth.

steps.title: Town clerk sends monthly list of deceased residents to the registrars of voters
steps.who: The city or town clerk in charge of death registration; residents 18 or older.

deadline.text: first day of every month and two days before every election

steps.summary: The list gives each decedent's ward, street and number so the registrars can remove them.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Householder and oldest next of kin must give notice within five days; the undertaker returns the certificate 'forthwith' and the burial permit requires it.

informantDuty.note: The householder and oldest next of kin must give notice; institutions report monthly; the undertaker returns the completed certificate to the board of health.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No review of every certificate, but every cremation or burial at sea requires a medical examiner's view and authorisation.

electronicRegistration.note: The state registrar's central database must be able to take entries from health professionals, funeral directors and the chief medical examiner, and clerks record deaths in it; the statute does not mandate exclusive electronic filing.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; deaths are recorded by town clerks in the state vital records database.

governmentPropagation.note: Recording a death automatically reaches the registrars of voters and the clerk of the home town. No statutory death feed to the RMV, Department of Revenue or MassHealth was found. Federal feeds are in us-federal.

certificateAccess.note: Restrictions in § 2A cover only out-of-wedlock and abnormal-sex births, fetal deaths and certain marriage records, so death records and certified copies are available to any applicant.

gaps: privateSectorVerification is left to the us-federal layer (LADMF); no Massachusetts-law route for banks or insurers beyond the open certified copy was found.

Open access to death certificates is inferred from § 2A listing no death-record restriction; no affirmative statute saying 'any person may obtain a death certificate' was read, and DPH Registry of Vital Records guidance on mass.gov was not fetched.
No statutory death feed to the Registry of Motor Vehicles (c. 90), Department of Revenue or MassHealth was found; those chapters were not searched in full.
Whether the Massachusetts electronic death registration system transmits to SSA is not stated in the statutes read; the federal side belongs in us-federal.
No statutory deadline in days for the undertaker's return ('forthwith') was found; 105 CMR regulations on death registration were not read.
